evidence.role: Initial ticket delivery and its callback occur inside the guarded, atomic purchase.
Safe mint updates ownership and then invokes the shared receiver acceptance check.
Recipient rejection or callback failure reverts safe delivery.
Burn and redemption-state writes share one transaction with prize or cash delivery, so delivery failure rolls them back.
Permissionless settlement is storage-only and does not depend on recipient cooperation.

searched.where: Five production files and all 31 dependency-hashes.json paths
searched.result: Read in full; SHA-256 verification matched 31/31 dependency hashes.
39 matches across seven files; all mint and safe-transfer receiver paths were traced through ERC721Utils.
135 matches across 11 files; every production recipient read, write, delivery, error, and event site was classified.
70 matches across ten files; direct transfer, safe transfer, NFT delivery, cash delivery, and failure branches were read.
57 matches across four files; modifier implementation, clone initial-slot behavior, inherited ownership updates, and burn sites were traced.
One production _safeMint call, four _transferQuote callers, two _settleWinningTicket callers, and all three inherited receiver-check call sites were read.

reasoning: Every path that executes ticket-recipient code uses the ERC-721 receiver check and cannot commit after rejection. Winner and refund delivery failures revert the same transaction containing burns and liability writes; settlement and other allocated claims do not require recipient cooperation. The inherited unsafe transfer branch invokes no recipient code, while the unguarded safe-transfer callback runs only after ownership is current and has no later economic write, so no uncovered branch makes the requirement partial.
